package.title: WS-push of new and deleted stories: live rings without a reload

specification.intent: Make the stories feed live: a dedicated /api/v1/ws/stories WebSocket channel (cookie auth + Origin check, no chat membership, ping/pong keepalive) backed by a user-keyed StoriesHub; POST /stories broadcasts story_created with a viewer-independent StoryResponse shape (viewed=False, is_own=False — true for every non-owner by construction) excluding the uploader, DELETE /stories/{id} broadcasts story_deleted to everyone; the frontend stories feature gains a singleton ws module over the UNMODIFIED WSTransport whose events reach StoriesController through a listener registry: story_created is mapped by the existing toStoryDto and inserted at the head of the others-unviewed group (id-dedupe), story_deleted removes the id — the chat page opens the socket on CDM next to fetchStories and the withStore-wrapped row re-renders in place.

requirements.title: Backend: stories WS channel with created/deleted fan-out
requirements.description: StoriesHub in backend/app/ws/hub.py keyed user_id -> set[WebSocket] (multi-socket per user, snapshot iteration with the ChatHub try/except + prune-stale policy, empty-set cleanup); /ws/stories endpoint in backend/app/ws/router.py copying the chat socket's structure (Origin allow-list -> sync _user_from_websocket -> accept -> hub connect -> receive loop answering only ping with the chat endpoint's exact pong frame -> finally disconnect; NO membership check, reject 1008); StoryService.to_broadcast_response(story, owner) with viewed=False/is_own=False over _common_fields(story, owner) shared with the list_feed mapper closure (the owner User is passed by the caller — create_story has current_user; never an owner-view mapper call); emission from the ENDPOINTS after commit (chat_deleted/reaction precedent): create_story broadcasts story_created with model_dump(mode='json') and exclude_user_id=current_user.id, delete_story broadcasts story_deleted {story_id} to everyone; no migration.
requirements.source: docs/NEXT.md priority 1 (WS-push of new stories); operator scope decision 2026-10-25: story_created + story_deleted

requirements.title: Frontend: live slice patches from the stories socket
requirements.description: Export the existing private toStoryDto from src/features/chats/stories/api/own.ts (it copies viewed/is_own verbatim and resolves fileUrl/avatarPoolUrl/alt); new src/features/chats/stories/ws/gateway.ts single-listener registry (the chats/ws/gateway.ts anti-cycle pattern) and ws/own.ts singleton over the UNMODIFIED WSTransport: ownStoriesUrl()=joinUrl(env.wsUrl,'/ws/stories'), idempotent connectStoriesSocket() with subscriptions registered before connect() and a failed connect swallowed/logged (never an unhandled rejection — the transport's bounded reconnect already retries), Message callback receives the already-parsed {type,content} and routes story_created/story_deleted (unknown types ignored), closeStoriesSocket() plus transport-Close nulling the module reference so a later CDM reconnects; StoriesController stays the sole writer of state.stories: constructor registers the listener, public connectStoriesSocket() delegates, handleStoryCreated maps + id-dedupes + inserts at countLeadingOwnStories(current) (head of the others-unviewed group; 0 when no own stories), handleStoryDeleted filters by story_id (absent -> no-op); chat page CDM calls connectStoriesSocket() right after fetchStories(); chat.test.ts adds connectStoriesSocket to the existing CDM stub convention (fetchChats/fetchStories stubs) so the 18 page tests never touch a real WebSocket, plus one assertion pinning the CDM call; no explicit logout close (chat-socket symmetry).

specification.goal: When any user uploads a story, every other connected client's stories row shows the new ring live; when a story is deleted, the ring disappears — no page reload, no refetch.
constraints: Layers downward only; guard-architecture --all --strict stays green; the stories ws module never imports the controller directly (listener registry), the controller never imports WSTransport.
WSTransport is reused UNMODIFIED (bounded reconnect, 5 s ping, explicit close never reconnects) — src/utils/WSTransport.ts and its test are forbidden writes.
The envelope {'type','content'} and the pong frame match the chat WS endpoint exactly; emissions come from endpoints after commit, never from the sync service layer.
The uploader is excluded from story_created per-user (all their sockets); story_deleted goes to everyone; the frontend id-dedupe keeps either policy safe.
No migration: alembic heads output must not change.
Existing suites stay green; test counts grow from the 322 mocha / 179 pytest baseline (4 ingestion-converter failures are pre-existing Windows specifics outside the write-set).
nonGoals: live updates while not on the chat page (socket opens on chat-page CDM; missed events converge on the next mount)
pushing story views to other clients
TTL-expiry pushes (a pushed story may expire server-side in a slice — same click behavior as a stale mount today)
opening the stories socket on login/registration pages
a stories unread badge (rings carry unreadness)
the owner's other tabs receiving story_created (broadcast-all is a one-line flip if ever wanted)
WS push for avatar changes, unread_counts consolidation, the main.ts duplicate GET /chats bootstrap tail (separate NEXT items)
specification.scope: backend ws hub/router, stories service and endpoints with their pytest; frontend stories feature (api mapper export, new ws module + tests, controller, chat page CDM) with mocha; docs/NEXT.md and the progress log.

criteria.title: Stories WS channel with fixed-shape fan-out
criteria.statement: /api/v1/ws/stories authenticates by the access cookie, enforces the Origin allow-list (reject 1008), requires no chat membership, answers ping with the chat endpoint's exact pong frame and ignores other inbound events; StoriesHub tracks sockets by user_id (multi-socket per user), prunes stale, cleans up on disconnect; POST /stories broadcasts story_created with viewed=False/is_own=False excluding the uploader, DELETE /stories/{id} broadcasts story_deleted {story_id} to everyone; emissions happen in the endpoints after commit; pytest covers auth rejection, foreign Origin, ping/pong, two-recipient fan-out, owner exclusion (frame order), disconnect cleanup and story_deleted; the unit test pins the invariant in executable form — to_broadcast_response(story, owner) equals the item list_feed(foreign_viewer_id) returns for that story (foreign viewer, no StoryView rows); alembic heads unchanged.

criteria.title: Live slice patches from the stories socket
criteria.statement: A story_created frame routed through the stories ws module (singleton WSTransport on /ws/stories, idempotent connect whose failure is swallowed/logged — never an unhandled rejection, subscriptions before connect, Close nulls the reference) reaches StoriesController as the sole writer of state.stories: duplicate id no-op, otherwise toStoryDto-mapped insertion at the head of the others-unviewed group (right after the own block, 0 when none); story_deleted removes the id (absent no-op); chat page CDM connects next to fetchStories() (pinned by an assertion; the 18 existing page tests stub connectStoriesSocket per the CDM stub convention so no unit test touches a real WebSocket) and the withStore row re-renders without a reload; WSTransport reused unmodified; mocha covers the ws module and the controller cases.

criteria.title: Gates and bookkeeping
criteria.statement: npm run verify passes (mocha grows from 322), the backend gate passes (179 passed baseline + new tests; the 4 ingestion-converter failures are pre-existing Windows specifics outside the write-set), guard-architecture --all --strict reports zero violations, alembic heads unchanged; progress log entry and NEXT.md priority 1 retired; one PR to dev; no file outside the manifest write-sets changes.

releaseImpact: Additive: one new WS endpoint and one new user-keyed hub (no chat WS protocol change), two new outbound event types on a dedicated channel, an exported mapper function, a new stories ws module and controller/page hooks; no router, auth, schema or deployment changes.
